answer: Dissolution keeps the clock: each identity seals one pearl, a pellet of key-fixed mass and composition, in standard umber suspension, dissolving at a rate its surface fixes. At set times auditors fire a light pulse through the vessel and read opacity against the umber baseline; readings must trace the curve recomputed from the pellet mass. One honest agent tends one vessel per epoch; a farm with 1,000 identities tends 1,000 vessels on 1,000 benches all epoch, because the rate will not hurry, and two names on one vessel share one curve and one dissolved mass, so neither shows a full trace.
